summary: t_hunted_source.py is a faithful, well-commented copy of lamley_source.py with the prescribed Blogger adaptations (h3.post-title, div.post-body, =sNNN path-stripped dedup). All 14 tests green; full repo suite (942 tests) passes with no regressions. SSRF allowlist matches lamley pattern 1:1, _notify helper is verbatim, filter_boilerplate runs BEFORE subtitle lift per the critical-order requirement. Three minor suggestions below — none blocking.

suggestions.suggestion: Regex deviation from tech-spec AC is broader than strictly necessary. Tech-spec AC literally locks `r'=s\d+(-c)?$'` (trailing only); shipped code is `r'=s\d+(-c)?(?:/|$)'` which matches the marker anywhere in the path, not just at end-of-string. The broadening is correct for Blogger's canonical mid-path shape (`=s1600/photo.jpg`) — the test `test_image_dedup_strips_blogger_size_suffix` provides the live evidence — and the comment block on lines 53-59 explicitly documents the deviation. However, the AC bullet in tasks/1.md remains worded for the narrower form. Either (a) keep code as-is and reword the AC bullet in tasks/1.md (line 102) to match shipped regex, or (b) add an explicit note in decisions.md so future readers see the AC vs code mismatch is intentional. Behaviour is correct; this is documentation hygiene only.
suggestions.benefit: Closes the AC-vs-code drift loop so the next reviewer (or a tech-spec re-read in 6 months) doesn't flag it as a spec violation.

suggestions.suggestion: File is 206 LOC vs the AC target ~130-170 LOC (hard ceiling 200). Overshoot is +6 LOC, all in docstrings/comments — executable code is 104 LOC, well under target. AC bullet in tasks/1.md line 95 explicitly permits 'до 200 — приемлемо если есть docstrings' so this is acceptance-compliant in spirit, but the literal '~130-170' phrasing on line 95 is now off. Trivially squeezable by collapsing the 8-line header docstring or the multi-line block comment at lines 53-59. Recommend leaving as-is — the docstring/comment density is genuinely useful for SSRF + regex-deviation context.
suggestions.benefit: If reviewers downstream interpret the AC strictly, a 6-line trim to the header docstring lands inside the 200 ceiling cleanly.

suggestions.suggestion: `assert 'Mais um lançamento...' not in out['paragraphs']` uses Python's `in` operator on a List[str], which is exact-element membership. This works because paragraphs is a list of full paragraph strings, but a future reader might assume substring containment (Python `in` on str does substring). Rename the assertion target variable or add a 1-line comment noting `paragraphs is a List[str], 'in' is exact-membership here`. Same comment applies on line 114 (positive containment assertion). Not a bug — current behaviour is what the test intends.
suggestions.benefit: Reduces confusion for the next reader scanning the assertion.

review_focus_answers.lamley_mirror_correctness: Confirmed 1:1. Signature `fetch_t_hunted_article(link, session=None, notifier=None) -> Optional[Dict]` matches `fetch_lamley_article` byte-for-byte. `_is_allowed_t_hunted_url` is a verbatim copy of `_is_allowed_lamley_url` (lamley_source.py:216-226) with constant + function-name swap. `_notify` (t_hunted_source.py:63-75) is a verbatim copy of lamley_source.py:199-206 with a proper type annotation added on the `notifier` parameter (improvement vs lamley's untyped version). Body-walk shape (lines 167-171) is identical to lamley_source.py:344-348. Cross-checked against lamley_source.py at HEAD.
review_focus_answers.image_dedup_correctness: Both shapes are covered. The shipped regex `r'=s\d+(-c)?(?:/|$)'` collapses (a) trailing `.../=s1600` (covered by `$` branch in alternation), (b) mid-path `.../=s1600/photo.jpg` (covered by `/` branch), and (c) `-c` cropped variants `=s320-c/...`. Test `test_image_dedup_strips_blogger_size_suffix` (lines 179-206) asserts photo1's =s1600 and =s640 variants collapse to one entry while photo2 with `-c` suffix stays separate. Manually verified all four cases with a regex playground — see review session log. ReDoS-safe (bounded `\d+`, no nested greedy quantifiers).
review_focus_answers.boilerplate_filter_call_ordering: Correct. `filter_boilerplate(paragraphs)` runs at line 177 BEFORE subtitle lift at line 181. Test `test_boilerplate_filter_applied_before_subtitle_lift` (lines 208-233) locks the order by injecting EN boilerplate `'Share on Facebook'` as the first paragraph and asserting the real lead becomes subtitle. Inline comment at lines 173-176 explicitly flags this as CRITICAL ORDER with the reason.
review_focus_answers.error_handling: All four error paths covered with `_notify` (logger.error + safe notifier call): (1) SSRF host-reject → admin_alerts.alert_t_hunted_host_rejected, return None (line 114-116); (2) HTTP/network error → admin_alerts.alert_t_hunted_fetch_error, return None (lines 126-131); (3) oversize body → logger.warning only, return None (lines 133-140) — alert intentionally omitted per the AC and inline comment, defensive gate; (4) missing body wrapper → admin_alerts.alert_t_hunted_no_body, return None (lines 163-165). raise_for_status() at line 125 catches HTTP 4xx/5xx into the same RequestException branch. Timeout is set via _TIMEOUT_SECONDS=15 (line 44).
review_focus_answers.deviation_3_admin_alerts_import: Reading t_hunted_source.py line 34: `import admin_alerts` — a module-level import of admin_alerts IS present in the production code, and the three call sites (lines 115, 129, 164) reference `admin_alerts.alert_t_hunted_*` by qualified name. This is NOT a deviation from THIS task's spec. The task's own spec authorizes this approach explicitly (tasks/1.md lines 22, 52, 157): 'В production-коде (`t_hunted_source.py`) обращаемся к `admin_alerts.alert_t_hunted_*` напрямую — это сработает после merge'а Task 2.' The 'dispatcher orchestrator' rule about avoiding admin_alerts builders applies to the news_bot wiring layer (Wave 2 Task 3), not the parser layer. Cross-file consistency: lamley_source.py uses the exact same direct-import pattern (`import admin_alerts` at lamley_source.py:27, calls to `admin_alerts.alert_lamley_*` throughout). Approach is correct and on-pattern.
review_focus_answers.code_style_consistency: Consistent with existing source modules. logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) at line 37 — standard pattern (matches lamley:29, mattel, orangetrack). Type hints on the public function signature (line 98-102) and on `_notify` (line 63) and `_is_allowed_t_hunted_url` (line 78) — actually richer than lamley_source.py:199 which leaves _notify untyped. Return shape `{title, subtitle, paragraphs, images}` matches lamley_source.py:374-379 (no `blocks` field — correct, Blogger posts are flat per architecture.md). Constants are private with underscore prefix (matches lamley convention for module-internal constants). Imports grouped stdlib → third-party → first-party with blank-line separators (PEP 8 style).
